name: Creation
about: The heavens declare the glory of God.

teachings.title: The heavens declare the glory of God
teachings.summary: Creation and conscience reveal God's power and law to all men so that they are without excuse, while His written word gives the hope of mercy and leads to salvation.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 19** is fairly short, yet packed with doctrine, teaching the purpose of creation, the testimony of God to all creatures, the picture of Christ, and the establishment of the law of the Lord in nature itself, that there is no excuse, while the believer is given constant reminders of His judgements.

**Romans 1:18–20**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse*

The heavens declare the glory of God. Looking upon the night sky we see His precision and power. And as the day follows day and night follows night, each with the passing of the sun and the stars, we are given evidence of His might.

The things of creation speak without words, that all man may understand. They don't need a language. They don't need to be explained. Man sees the passage of time, seasons, years, decades even, in heavenly bodies.

The vain hypothetical of a savage on a remote island, never hearing the gospel, is undone by the understanding that all nature is a parable and a testament of God, showing men truth.

The boldness of the sun breaking forth in the morning is as the risen Christ, returning in glory, a picture of the Creator Who is blessed forever, amen.

Nature teaches us God's law. His ways.

**1 Corinthians 11:14**
*Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him?*

His wrath is revealed against those who sin, even without the oracles of God documenting His commandments. The Spirit showing mankind the results of their transgressions. The understanding that murder, adultery, lying, stealing, all of these things that do harm to your neighbor and are a shame before God, are known.

**Romans 2:11–16**
*For there is no respect of persons with God. For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law; (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified. For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;) In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.*

Man can see the law of God, know it written in their hearts, watch the outcome of their behavior and the wrath upon those who sin, and know they are guilty before the consuming fire which is God.

How much more are we who have His statutes and commandments by the oracles of God?

**Romans 3:1–2**
*What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.*

The advantage given Israel, and held by the Jews in Paul's day, is now given to the world. That everyone may know His word.

*The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple.*

If the day declares His righteousness and the night His knowledge, and the very nature of things speaks to His wrath, then the oracles of God give us the hope of His mercy. God is a rewarder to those that diligently seek Him.

The fear of the Lord is clean, and known to all men. The fool may say in their heart there is no God, but the wise fear Him, even if they don't know scripture.

The truth is more desirable than gold, sweeter than honey. Its pursuit is its own reward, spurring us to seek Him. The warnings and rewards, motivation to learn His ways.

And, in that knowledge, we find His word, and from that word, salvation.

teachings.title: All creation is a parable
teachings.summary: Creation is a parable that shows God's might and love, and believers, as new creatures, are meant to declare His glory to the heathen like the heavens do.
teachings.text:
We are blessed to have the knowledge of the truth before us. His inspired and preserved word, that we may know Him. And God does not leave those without the oracles lacking.

But for the children of God, creation gives us reassurance and opportunities to worship Him for His might and glory. To have reminders that He loves us.

To every seed we sow that comes to fruition. To every shooting star, or bird in flight, or wave crashing on the shore, we are able to look at the Lord in awe. Babies born to the death of the elderly, spring following winter, the setting sun and darkest night...all creation is a parable to those with ears to hear and eyes to see.

To know God loves us. And His mercy upon us is evidence to others seeking truth. The light in us shines that others may see and glorify God.

We are to be as the firmament, as the rising sun and the crashing wave. His children are meant to teach the heathen who seeks the Lord, as much as anything in creation. Because we are new creatures in Christ, brought forth as a testimony to God's greatness.

*Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.* Amen

teachings.title: The wild beasts under His providence
teachings.summary: God's questions about the wild creatures show that what man cannot control or understand is ordered by God's providence, and man, wild and stubborn like them, is sustained by His mercy.
teachings.text:
The Lord continues to speak to Job out of the whirlwind. Job, His servant, seeks to know why he has been afflicted. But God challenges him to see the things that His providence delivers. The grand scheme. The big picture.

That for all the wisdom the Lord has given man, and the ability of man to apply it for their lives, there is so much more that is beyond our control, but not His.

God asks Job to consider the wild goats, the wild ass, the unicorn - which isn't a one horned mythical beast, but the wild oxen, the strong bull or aurochs as it was known, the ostrich or the horse. The hawk and the eagle.

Man doesn't control or understand the time of the goat, when they calve. Unlike the tame goats, they, without any aid or midwifery, bring forth their kids in sorrow, and cast them out to fend for themselves. And God provides.

The wild ass is free. God has given it liberty in the wilderness, and a stubborn rebellion against being controlled by men. He searches the mountains for his food, and while it doesn't starve, it isn't fed as a tamed donkey would be.

The unicorn, or wild bull, doesn't serve man, or tread out the corn. It doesn't reside in a stable. It can't be trusted with the work of the tamed oxen. But it lives.

God gives goodly wings to the peacock, which cannot fly. And wings and feathers to the ostrich, which not only cannot fly, but runs in the wilderness, dropping her eggs to be hatched in the sand and sun. Not protected in a nest, but exposed to being crushed or broken and eaten. And yet, they don't go extinct. God provides, even as He withheld wisdom and understanding to the big dumb bird, giving her speed to outrun man, even on horseback.

The ways and whys of creation don't always make sense to man, and are often well out of our control, and yet it continues on, in His ways.

Like the beasts, man is a wild thing, marrying, and bringing forth children. Stubborn and strong willed. Even at liberty, prone to wander, God provides.

The rain that brought forth green vegetation in the wilderness, and it becomes the food the wild beasts survive on.

The horse, whose strength man has harnessed, did not gain its strength from men. It can be startled by a grasshopper, but charge into battle, the noise of armed men, and the shield and spear rattling against him, the trumpet sounding as it rides headlong towards death.

The hawk flies towards the south, soaring in the warm winds, without our instruction. The eagle nests in the castles of mountains, and seeks prey afar off. Not by will of man. Her chicks go where corpses lay, and feast.

In all this, man is helpless. It is all the providence of God.

But we are like these same beasts. We go about our lives, having children that will grow and go off. Stubborn to instruction, refusing to be driven where we should go. Forsaking the blessings of being a servant to God, in exchange for His mercies and bare sustenance in the wilderness.

All things exist as He made them. And the systems in place for a reason.

Man, who is frightened of thunder and who can't be trusted to do what's right, who runs after war, who abanons their own kin to the wastes of life, who feeds on the dead, our wisdom is not sufficient to explain our nature, or how it mirrors those wild beasts we can't comprehend. But to God, and to His point of view, it is all in order.

teachings.title: Job asks why, God shows Who
teachings.summary: God answers Job's why by enlarging his view of Who God is, showing creatures that flourish under His care through suffering and danger without being abandoned.
teachings.text:
God's speech from the whirlwind is a humbling reminder of divine providence over creation, far beyond human control or full comprehension. **Job 39** portrays wild creatures thriving under God's care, even in ways that seem precarious or counterintuitive to us, underscoring His sovereignty while highlighting our own limitations and rebellious tendencies. Like these wild creatures, we often wander in stubborn liberty, forsaking full submission, yet God sustains us in mercy.

We behave in ways that should result in our extinction. And yet, God's mercies are extended to us in ways we don't even notice or comprehend.

In all these, suffering, danger, apparent neglect, and death are woven into the fabric of life, yet the creatures flourish under God's hand. None of it is explained to them. None of it is micromanaged by man. And none of it indicates that God has abandoned His creation.

Job is asking "why?" But God is showing him "Who." By enlarging Job's view of God, and the order He created, He is answering Job, just not in the way Job intended.

teachings.title: All creation testifies of His power
teachings.summary: Job teaches that the heavens, earth and seas show God's power and glory to all men, so that by the things that are made they are without excuse (Romans 1, Psalm 19).
teachings.text:
Following Bildad's short speech on the Holiness of God compared to man, and undeserving of redemption (which had allusions to Christ, even in his doubt), Job answers.

He asks how has he helped others in need? Those without power, without strength, without wisdom? A man may answer of themselves, but Job makes it clear, it is of God.

Man doesn't speak things into creation, or give spirit and life. Man doesn't have the power of God, which all creation testifies. There is nothing kept from Him and yet, man is left with such little understanding of the Lord.

Job says all the wonders and miracles of creation are just a glimpse, and the thunder of His power, who can understand?

The dialogue has begun to transition from talking about Job as if he were a heathen, sinful, ignorant and scornful of God and His ways, to Job instructing the three men of the nature of God, salvation and creation, which is a parable offered to all men, plain to see.

The stars in the heavens, the earth in space, the oceans and land that bound the waters, all speak of His power and glory.

**Romans 1:18-20**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse*

**Psalm 19:1-3**
*The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork. Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge.There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.*

teachings.title: All creation testifies of God
teachings.summary: Against Zophar, Job shows that God reveals Himself through creation so every man knows Him, and He rules life, wisdom and nations.
teachings.text:
Job responds to Zophar the Naamathite, and his assertions that none can know the ways of God, His secret things. That all that Zophar knows is that Job deserved what he received and more, God should have done worse to him.

But this was pontificating nonsense. God reveals Himself to man in innumerable ways. In sundry times and diverse manners.

All creation testifying, a parable of God.

**Romans 1:18-20**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse.*

And so Job answers this claim. He says, surely they have a wisdom, as men, and as men, it will die with them, but he has understanding as well. He isn't inferior to them in knowledge, and Job says they are not giving him profound arguments, but things everyone knows. Obvious truths and natural man wisdom.

Many will say banal and vain words, of basic truths and pass it off as great wisdom when they are looking to be holier than thou hypocrites.

We see it all the time: "Jesus said not to judge!" they'll say, while judging the righteous for preaching the whole word of God. For preaching standards and separation.

Job says he's like the upright man that is scoffed at by his neighbor for calling upon God. Peter wrote about scoffers in the last days, just as Noah was scoffed at in his day. People mocking faith is a constant in the believer's life.

A man who is in tribulation is hated too. As Job describes it, a man ready to slip with his feet, being as hated as a lamp or a light to a person at ease, who is resting. People who are comfortable don't want to deal with people in need. They resent them.

Those that provoke God, and mock faith may seem to get away with it and even be given abundance. But look upon creation and see the truth. Every man knows God is real and all creation testifies His wrath and nature and truth.

Wisdom comes to the elderly by the exposure and experience in God's creation. Length of days leads to knowledge and wisdom, and understanding of God's counsel.

God gives life and breath. He breaks things down, corrupts and decays, and nothing can bring it back. He causes drought and flood. He even gives to the deceived strong delusion.

He sets up judges and deliverers and kings and princes, and leads the same to ruin.

Just as long life gives wisdom, He takes away the understanding of the aged. Senility and dementia are His to give, just as the knowledge and wisdom were.

God controls the fates of nations, reveals secrets. He causes the people to wander in the wilderness. To grope in the dark, all to teach us of His wonderful light.

teachings.title: The chronogenealogies and a young earth
teachings.summary: The ages in Genesis 5 and 11 are given literally and, with the generations to Christ, place the earth at about 6,000 years old.
teachings.text:
For my autistic brothers in Christ, this is 1,558 years from Adam to Shem.

The chronogenealogies of Genesis 5 are given to provide times and understanding of the human nature of man, and to provide the direct lineage from Adam to Noah and his sons.

Long-lived though they may have been, they lived, had children and died*. They populated the earth. They all sinned whether sons of God or sons of man, whether they called upon the name of the Lord or rejected His salvation.

But they lived and these were the span of years from creation to Noah and his sons.

Biblical authority and fundamentalism should rest on rightly dividing the word of God, and taking what's given literally as literal, and what's parable, a picture or a symbol as figurative. These ages are given literally.

It is odd how those who take the figurative literally, such as the Nicodemuses who gets caught up in misunderstood false doctrine taken from parables, almost invariably take the literal as symbolic, and most reject the specific accounting of years from creation to flood, to Christ.

And so, taking the Bible literal where it's given to us literally, and going from **Genesis 5** to **Genesis 11:32**, we get to Shem's descendant Terah, father of Abraham. Adding all of the provided years gives us a time span of about 2,008 years from Adam to Abraham.

And from **Matthew 1**, we are given the generations from Abraham to Jesus Christ.

*So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations.*

The total of these generations isn't as precise but adds up to roughly 2,000 years to the first coming of the Messiah.

As far as the Bible goes, we have recorded the rough years from creation to Christ, given, inspired and preserved by God. The time from Christ to now, the anno domini so to speak, well, that could be roughly 2022 years. It may not be. Missing time, garbled calendars, i's for 1's...I can't say. The calendar is not the preserved word of God. (I lean towards some centuries being faked and it being less time from Christ to now, but it's all speculation)

But taking the given ~2020 years that is commonly accepted, this places the earth at just slightly more than 6,000 years old. Give or take a century or two.

I have never seen anything convincing that suggests otherwise, through all the science so-called, and theories and theologies of man. In fact, given time, the wisdom of man invariably fails and is changed to fit new secular theories, unfalsifiable as they are.

But God's word is the rock of our salvation, that we as believers build our faith and our lives upon. Unchanged and unchangeable.

teachings.title: A literal creation about 6,000 years ago
teachings.summary: Genesis 1 is a literal account of creation about 6,200 years ago because God who cannot lie says so, and evolution is worship of time, a created thing.
teachings.text:
Now, note the order of things. This is how all of creation was made. And the creation of days, separated from night, morning and evening, was created by God who is outside of time.

The fullness of the Godhead exists when nothing else did, including time, and through Him was created light, substance, life, and mankind. Everything after its own kind, with the seed contained therein propagating that life over time.

This is a literal story of creation, as it occurred roughly 6,200 years ago.

Not because of fossils found in weird places, or the problems with carbon dating, or the position of the stars in the firmament unchanging, or the complexity and variance of life.

But because God said this is how it happened. In His inspired and preserved word, The God who cannot lie tells us these things and that they are so.

Evolution, which is the worship of time, or Kronos as the creator, is literally the worship of the created, as we see in Genesis, because God created time. And so we know it's false.

Biblical inerrancy, and the fundamentalist belief that it is the inspired and preserved word of God, has yet to fail, even as science falsely so-called makes claims to the contrary, God's hand is revealed continually making the wise into fools.

This is why God's word is continually under attack. This is why doubt is continually sown. Because, if many have doubts about any aspect of God's word, then many will not believe the report. The Gospel, and will perish as sinners.

And while you don't have to necessarily believe in the literal biblical creation in order to believe that Jesus is the son of God who died for our sins and was resurrected again, and whom through which we are given Grace by God unto eternal life, it is difficult to then express that Faith to others while doubting much of His word. Or thinking it allegory, or some sort of parable.

The gospels give account back to Adam. The genealogies are there to mark time. And the generations from Noah back to Adam, from Abraham back to Noah, from Israel to Christ... These are there for a purpose.

And while there are some seeking to take away from God's word by casting doubt not just on the creation story but on every biblical text that draws upon it, all scripture that refers to it in describing Jesus Christ to us, there are people that seek to add to his word as well. It is easy to read into it things that are not there, and this too is an error.

So as we go forth through Genesis understand that it is not only the faith of this author, but my firm opinion that the Bible is literally true, and the truths revealed from Genesis 1 through the end in Revelation 22, is the story of Jesus Christ. God revealing His Son to us that we may believe and have eternal life.

It is God's word, His testimony, the testaments that He has given us to His promise for us. And from start to finish, Alpha to Omega it is one gospel, the good news of salvation through Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: Evolution versus the testimony of creation
teachings.summary: Evolution is unfalsifiable science falsely so-called, while biblical creation, God's testimony, explains the kinds, complexity and origin of nations.
teachings.text:
The disproved theory of Evolution of the species, which has become unfalsifiable nonsense requiring increasingly foolish leaps, requiring the constant changing of factors like time frame, scale, etc as each presents a problem. Rather than abandoning the theory, adherents simply say the natural observations and assumptions that disprove it must be wrong. Including the math of time and adaptation that definitively debunks it.

Meanwhile, Biblical creation is proved as the testimony of God, and explains the kinds and types, impossible adaptations, incredible beauty, complexity of systems and gives us a true accounting of the origin of race and nations, and the boundaries and habitations thereof.

Nonbelievers have faith in science, falsely so-called and the theories of Jews and Masons and Jesuits that tickle their ears and appeal to their conceits, so much so that the shifting narratives used to buttress it fail to even elicit a blip of cognitive dissonance.

teachings.title: Two trees in Eden
teachings.summary: Reads Genesis 2:8-10 as God giving man two options from the beginning, the tree of knowledge of good and evil, the law, and the tree of life, which is by faith in God's word.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 2:8-10**
*And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed. And out of the ground made the LORD God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.  And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.*

From the beginning God gave two options to the man He had created; the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, the law, and the tree of life, which is by faith in the word of God.

teachings.title: The birds were gleaning
teachings.summary: Tells how birds that kept pests out of his garden were eating his peas, and how the Spirit reminded him of gleaning and that the ox that treads out the corn is not muzzled. Ends with his frustration gone and praise for God's garden.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 19:9-10**

*And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest. And thou shalt not glean thy vineyard, neither shalt thou gather every grape of thy vineyard; thou shalt leave them for the poor and stranger: I am the LORD your God.*

***Deuteronomy 24:19-21**

*When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that the LORD thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hands. When thou beatest thine olive tree, thou shalt not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow. When thou gatherest the grapes of thy vineyard, thou shalt not glean it afterward: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.*

Keep this in mind.

So this year the garden has been very good to us, we've been blessed with healthy plants and few diseases. The harmful insects have been kept to a minimum thanks to so many birds nesting in and around the chicken coop. We added some birdhouses last year, and so far this year they have been phenomenal in keeping harmful bug population to almost zero.

The peas did exceptionally well this year, and produced over 6 gallon bags of pods of big, delicious sweet peas. Normally the plants have died off by this point but, despite the heat and the drought like conditions, several of the vines are still healthy and producing, and there are even new flowers forming daily as it crawls across the trellis. It's providing noontime shade for my massive cukes and cherry tomatoes.

I had harvested the last big batch about a week and a half ago, and I was letting the stragglers develop before taking them as well.

But then I began to notice discarded pea shells all around the bush of vines.

The same day I noticed a baby chipmunk run across the yard away from the peas.

Of course I assumed that was the culprit. I set traps and threw mothballs throughout the yard coffee grounds, peppermint spray. 

The traps never triggered, and the pea pods kept falling, chewed open and hollowed out.

Naturally I redoubled my efforts and, still, no joy. More and more dead pods littering the ground.

So today I stopped and just watched for a while, a little frustrated, and asking God for protection from the vermin. To extend the hedge.

As I'm praying, talking to God, I see that the birds, the same birds who all year have been keeping the harmful bugs away from my plants, feasting on peas. 

They took out an early infestation of Denver potato beetles. I found maybe three Beatles one day crushed them, and then watched birds decimate them over the next week.

Beetles that attacked my squash and cucumbers last year, did not make a reappearance and a white fly infestation at my cabbage was swiftly dealt with. 

It was those same birds, coming through my pea patch and eating all my peas.

God said to me "they're gleaning." The Spirit reminding me of the practice, bringing all things into remembrance. A laborer gets its reward. *Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn.*

And, just like that my Elmer Fudd frustration disappeared.

Of course this means next year I probably have to net them early.

Easily 10' high and climbing. The cuke is going up the tomatoes and beans going up that.

This is God's garden.

teachings.title: Creation is the parable
teachings.summary: Reflects from gardening that all of creation is a parable pointing to biblical truth. Says it is not that parables use creation to explain God's word, but that creation exists to illustrate it.
teachings.text:
I put up a few bird houses in the midst of the garden, two years ago. Now we have nests of robins, wrens, chickadees, sparrows, cardinals and jays all around the yard, in trees and shrubs.

The chickens likely help attract them too, with cast off food and a constant source of water. 

Together, wild and fowl flock have made my garden mostly bad bug free. Praise God.

When you grow things you really get to appreciate creation, and the intricacies and complexity of the systems and God's amazing work that goes into taking a seed, planting it, watering it and reaping it. 

Literally all of creation is the parable to direct us to its true meaning. It's the revealed will of God being explained by literally all living things.

It's not that parables use creation to explain God's word. Creation *is* the parable. It exists to illustrate the biblical truth. Not the other way around.

teachings.title: The cornerstone laid before the foundation
teachings.summary: God's answer from the whirlwind points to Christ the chief cornerstone laid at creation, the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world, with the sons of God being believers rather than angels.
teachings.text:
*Then the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind.*..

The storm that gathered as Elihu spoke, which the boy used as it came to lecture Job with what he thought was profound wisdom, brings with it the voice of God. And He sets to immediately show the shallowness of Elihu and the three friends' thinking.

*Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?*

What a terrifying moment, to know that God will demand answers of you. And this fear should grip all men, that they believe on Christ, to avoid that fierce judgment, where all will be asked of those not found in His book of Life, by the omnipotent God of all.

He laid the foundations of the earth, the breadth and scope of creation was measured out by Him. The foundations of the world are set by Him, and the cornerstone thereof.

*Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.*..

**1 Peter 2:6-8**
*Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded. Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.*

The morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy and the truth of Jesus Christ, the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. The cornerstone laid, upon Which all is built.

(I believe this is a OT prophecy of Christ, Who has been since before creation, but Who IS and was born of men, to die and rise again. That the stars are the hosts of Heaven. That the sons of God are those from Adam who believed. Some think this is literally creation, and so the sons of God must be angels, to whom at no time did God call sons, according to scripture.)

From the seas to the shores to the heights of the sky, to the position of the stars in the sky, God has set all things, and the paths thereof.

The wonder of creation is not only in the placement of these things God created, but in their paths and purposes. Time itself is a testimony of His power.

The day chasing away the darkness. The rivers carrying the floodwaters to the sea. The voice of thunder, and the rain upon the wilderness, making it spring to life. The pictures of God's mercy and wrath, revealed. Made manifest that no man has an excuse.

Only God can create these things, and not as man would, even if we could. For the Lord knows the beginning from the end. The order He has made is greater than our ability to comprehend.

Creation isn't like the birth of man. Flood waters are pictured in birth, but is not the birth. There is no womb that could create the frost. The hail which will be used in due time by the Lord in His wrath. Rain isn't called and lightning ordered and arrayed, but by the living God.

God has even put what we call the food chain in its place, that the beasts of the world eat, even as they don't sow or reap. But that He opens death to all, that they may eat.

And this same God puts wisdom in man's heart.

teachings.title: The Septuagint chronology problem
teachings.summary: Points out that the Greek chronology of Lamech and Methuselah would have Methuselah living past the Flood.
teachings.text: The Septuagint forgery has a major problem. The Greek chronology says Lamech was 188 years old when Noah was born, so from Lamech's birth to the Flood was 188 + 600, or 788 years. But claims Methuselah lived 802 years after Lamech's birth. This means he lived for years after the Flood. Which is stupid and anyone using it is an idiot.

teachings.title: Scofield's gap theory from Jeremiah 4
teachings.summary: Scofield invented the gap theory between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2 from Jeremiah 4, so if he added to the first verse, none of his notes should be trusted.
teachings.text:
Scofield used his notes, interrupting the text of Scripture itself, column notes and foot notes, to add commentary and invent doctrine out of thin air.

Even today, a century later, this toxic corruption has infiltrated a majority of evangelical and many Baptist churches. Just as Judaizers had already taken root in Protestant sects and their seminaries, Scofield was the foot in the door to Bible colleges and KJVO churches.

But the heresies of C. I. Scofield were evident in the first chapter of the first book in the opening verses of the Bible.

In Genesis 1, he interrupts God's creation, to invent the idea that between verse 1;  *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.*

And verse 2 *And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.*

That there was a span of an earlier creation, that millions or billions of years passed. That there was a "gap," between the initial creation, and the ultimate creation, and that this was proved by the vision of Jeremiah in chapter 4:23-26.

He claims that this passage "clearly indicates" that the earth had undergone a "cataclysmic change as a result of divine judgement." That we could see evidence of this pre-Eden, pre-Adamic destruction. That Jeremiah was seeing a vision of this past event. That this would match the geologists of the era, and their theories of the earth being billions of years old. That the earth wasn't made fully formed and stocked with life, but that God had made it before as habitations for angels, who fell, and was destroyed and left void and without form until he renewed creation for Eden.

The Gap theory was very popular for a time in American Evangelical circles, but is almost universally rejected today by believing Christians, despite their continued use of the Scofield, and acceptance of other heresy he taught.

But if he is inventing things in the first verse of the first chapter. Why do they trust anything else he wrote?

teachings.title: The wrath of God revealed from heaven
teachings.summary: God reveals His wrath through creation and conscience so all are without excuse, and those who hold the truth in unrighteousness and worship the creature have their hearts darkened.
teachings.text:
So, in our prior instalment we see the righteousness of God is revealed to man through those that are saved sharing the Gospel of God in Christ Jesus with others. Here we see that God also reveals His nature, His wrath, from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men.

Their literal unrighteousness is part of His wrath. Man is punished by their own sin. We see it all the time, that the consequences of sin is a curse, teaching the wages of sin is death. Nature has revealed to us this truth, the system of consequence. We see it in the downfall of our own current society. We see the effects of sin in our own lives.

Because that which may be known of God is manifest in those who hold the truth in unrighteousness. God has shown men His judgment.

Man has a conscience. The law of God is written in our hearts. The Spirit has come to convict men of sin that they may know they need salvation. The law worked in the OT times to do the same, as a schoolmaster to our unrighteousness that we may seek salvation in the Lord.

These invisible things of God are visible, clearly seen, from the creation of the world through now. And His wrath is understood by His creation. Man understands right from wrong, as Paul gets into later in Romans.

We see His power and destruction in nature. We see it in the flood. In Sodom and Gomorrah. The judgment of nations.

We see the eternal power of the Godhead and so, all men are without excuse.

But men that knew God through His revelation, weren't thankful to God and didn't glorify Him as God, but became vain in their imaginations. Men knowing the judgment and wrath of God made up stories to explain it. Devised often complex systems of works and worship of idols to justify their sin. Vain, meaning unprofitable and a waste of time. Even today they invent a false god out of the Biblical God, and their perverse version of Jesus, while ignoring the truth of His judgment.

These people, the Bible says, have their foolish hearts darkened. Hardened. They become worse with time, clinging to their vain beliefs and not recognizing the truth of God through His revelations to us.

Prophets. His word. His power. The Gospel. His wrath. These things are given that all men seeking truth shall find it.

But those who became vain in their imaginations, whose foolish hearts are darkened, who profess themselves wise become fools, and change the glory of an uncorruptible God into idols, images made like unto corruptible man, like the Catholic church or the Orthodox that split off it. Or like unto birds, and animals and creeping things. Worship of nature. Worship of themselves even.

Worship of the created more than the Creator.

Because of all that...well, Paul tells us what ends up happening to these people in the following verses.

teachings.title: Satan was created, and the gap theory is false
teachings.summary: Quotes Ezekiel 28 and teaches that Satan is a created being, not a balance to God, and that the gap theory is a false doctrine since God called His finished creation very good. Traces Satan's fall, Hell prepared for the devil and his angels, and the plan of salvation in the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.
teachings.text:
**Ezekiel 28**

*12 Son of man, take up a lamentation upon the king of Tyrus, and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord God; Thou sealest up the sum, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty.

13 Thou hast been in Eden the garden of God; every precious stone was thy covering, the sardius, topaz, and the diamond, the beryl, the onyx, and the jasper, the sapphire, the emerald, and the carbuncle, and gold: the workmanship of thy tabrets and of thy pipes was prepared in thee in the day that thou wast created.

14 Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth; and I have set thee so: thou wast upon the holy mountain of God; thou hast walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire.

15 Thou wast perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee.

16 By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned: therefore I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God: and I will destroy thee, O covering cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire.

17 Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness: I will cast thee to the ground, I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee.

18 Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities, by the iniquity of thy traffick; therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee, and I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee.

19 All they that know thee among the people shall be astonished at thee: thou shalt be a terror, and never shalt thou be any more.*

**Ephesians 6:12**
*For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.*

**Isaiah 14**
*
12 How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!

13 For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north:

14 I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.*

Keeping in mind who Lucifer is, Satan. That old serpent. 

Knowing that the rulers of this world are given over to him. But it is important to note the Bible teaches that Satan is a created being. Satan was created by God. There was a day where Satan was created. The Heaven and the Earth was created in the 1st day so Satan was created in that first day. 

Some believe the devil is some sort of balance to God, or the Mormons say Jesus 'brother. These are blasphemous statements. Satan is a creature, Jesus the Creator. 

There is a false doctrine called the "Gap theory" that claims, among other things that Satan fell during creation week. That some time, millions of years in fact, passed between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2. And that in those millions of years a world was created, and fell, because of Satan and the 3rd of hosts that fell with him. 

It's a silly doctrine. We know that when God looks at His creation after His work was done, that He found it was "very good." Perfect. Complete. 

Not *very good* *other than the botched world and fallen angels. *

But Satan fell before Eve took of the apple. Iniquity was found in him, and many believe it was the love of man by God that did it. 

When Satan fell, and brought his murderous lie to Eve, casting doubt on God's word, he was attempting to place God in a difficult position with His beloved creation of man. 

We see in **Matthew 25:41** that Hell was created for Satan and the others who rebel with him. 

*Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.*

And knowing his ultimate fate at the judgment of the Lord, earned by his own inequities, he sought to bring down man with him. 

But God, having seen beginning to the end, knowing all things, being the exalted creator, already had a plan of salvation for fallen man. The lamb slain before the foundation of the world. Jesus Christ. And those who called upon the name of the Lord, gave He the power to became Sons of God, given eternal life. Heirs to an eternal kingdom. 

And His beloved mankind turned to a nation like unto the sand, or the stars. Filling up Heaven. Death defeated. Hell and Satan and all unbelieving, cast into the lake of fire, where the smoke of their torment rises forever. 

And Satan's ultimate defeat is known to him. And so, he goes before God, among the sons of God to accuse us, night and day. Like a ravenous lion seeking whom he may devour. Biting at the heel of Christ, who in turn crushes his head.

teachings.title: The day of the Lord is darkness to the damned
teachings.summary: Quotes Amos 5:18 to show that the day of the Lord is darkness and not light for those who desire it without God. Says believers are of the day and the light, and that day and night are a picture of this, a parable of creation.
teachings.text:
What ends do the damned have on the day of the Lord? They get darkness. Sun and moon and stars. 

We are of the day and of the light.

In fact one of the reasons God created day and night, if not the only reason, perhaps. It's a picture of this very thing at the end. That we understand the night and the day, the darkness and the light.

So we have that understanding when we hear God's word say it, we can picture it, and in picturing it understand what God's saying. The parable of creation

teachings.title: Primary doctrine and incidental opinions
teachings.summary: Says a belief is not Biblical doctrine unless scripture clearly spells it out, separating primary doctrines such as literal creation from secondary matters like the exact age of the earth. Urges not becoming dogmatic over the firmament or other worldly things, and hearing sound doctrine from preachers who hold the gospel of grace alone.
teachings.text:
Just because you believe something about the world to be true, doesn't make it Biblical doctrine. It actually has to be clearly spelled out in scripture, and even then other than the Gospel and a few primary doctrines, there's interpretation of secondary and tertiary doctrine that's open for discussion and then there are things people try to get the Bible to comment on that it simply doesn't. 

Literal creation is a primary doctrine. Biblical age as determined by generations is secondary. Earth being precisely 6,482 years old is interpretation that has Biblical basis, but is incidental, bearing no real importance in our spiritual walk, and good faith people of faith can disagree. 

Too many place their own beliefs of incidental and worldly things far to high in the order of importance.

Many, many, many of the people in our circles, especially young men who are aimless, lost, broken by trauma, or babes in Christ and culturally Christian but not quite there yet, need to hear hard preaching on sin and practical application of Biblical truths to their spiritual life and walk with Christ, from preachers who adhere to the Gospel of salvation by faith alone, in grace alone, plus nothing, minus nothing. 

And that preacher's idea or opinion of worldly things differing from your own shouldn't be a hindrance from hearing sound doctrine of spiritual things. 

If it is, you need to reevaluate what's important to you.

My preference for Easton's definition of Firmament in the Bible, over Nave's or Smith's, or even Webster's, doesn't make it doctrine. Simple as. 

It could just be the expanse, the reach of the heavens. "Firm" being in the word doesn't make it solid, even if I believe it to be. 

Don't project your opinions of the worldly onto scripture and become dogmatic in things that are ultimately not important. 

Sons of Belial, Jews and reprobates, being liars and leading persecution and engaging in subversion is true, because the Bible tells us so, explicitly. We don't have to prove they lie about the shape of the earth, or space, or age of creation, etc to prove they lie. Examples are simply signs to read, and the truth to ponder and wonder about.
